methodologyNote: Many-to-one (inbound: arrive by target, latest possible departure), as Liverpool and Sheffield. Historical source: a 23-page excerpt (printed pages 12A-42A, with gaps) of a Birmingham Corporation Tramways & Omnibus Department guide, dated c.1929 from internal evidence. Transcribed: every printed departure of the 15 Corporation bus services in the excerpt, used verbatim (services whose pages fall in the excerpt's gaps are missing or partial), with their fare stages and timing points geocoded as stops; the numbered tram route list and termini (p13A); and the fare stages of tram routes 86 and 87 (p12A). Modelled: the excerpt has no tram timetables, so every tram headway and running time is modelled. Tram running times come from the 1927 statutory speed schedule applied over the surveyed KMZ track and fitted to official 1930s journey times for 37 routes; tram headways are researched defaults (every 5 min peak and 8 min off-peak on main routes, short workings every 10 min in the peaks) calibrated to the 1929-30 tram car-miles, and occasional services are left out. Trolleybus route 7 (Nechells) is modelled too (10 mph and every 4 min in the peaks, from a 1922 description of the route; every 6 min off-peak, from the 1929-30 trolleybus mileage). Bus running times are inferred from the timetables' own turnaround offsets (the Outer Circle from its printed timing points; three services with no usable offsets use a speed model fitted to the others). Midland Red services and the 1929 railways are not included, which understates 1929 accessibility on those corridors. Modern feed is GB rail + England bus (DfT BODS, including West Midlands Metro and the Air-Rail Link) for a Wednesday in October 2026, filtered to a 30 km radius; coach services are excluded. Trams-only mode compares against today's rail + Metro (and the Air-Rail Link), buses-only (which includes the trolleybus) against today's buses. Transfer penalty 5 min per change (the low end of published interchange valuations, about 5-18 min; sensitivity at 1 and 10 min in the stress-test report). No coastline clipping (inland city).

robustness.basis: the project's own variant feeds (tram model faster and slower, headways higher and lower, occasional services)

routes.name: Outer Circle (Service 11)
routes.linkLabel: Printed timetable, page 27A
routes.sourceText: Birmingham Corporation Tramways & Omnibus Department guide, c.1928-30, printed page 27A; running times from the printed timing-point departures (full circuit 140 min): each trip follows its bus, linked across the six timing-point lists, and passes the timing points at the printed times (95.7% of 15,690 timing-point passes); where the bus is missing from the next list (a print inconsistency, mostly at the changes between 7- and 10-minute headways) the trip carries on at the inferred segment time (677 passes). Between timing points the stops are timed by the tram kinematics at the scale that makes the expected running time equal the printed interval: cruise 10.6-20.0 mph, never above the 20 mph legal limit, calling at 40-100% of intermediate stops (21 of 78 distinct printed intervals need fewer than every call)
